transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I just keep forgetting things. Basic adult stuff, mostly. 

Like, I keep forgetting to pay my bills, or... returning emails for interviews. I miss appointments a lot. Or I just don't follow through on normal errands. It's... it's starting to cost me real opportunities, so... yeah. That's why I came in.
How long have you been experiencing these memory and organizational problems? Have they been happening your whole life, or is this something that started more recently?

Um... I guess it's been really bad for about a year and two months. It, um... it started around the time things kind of fell apart at my biotech job. And... it just kept happening after I was fired from there. So... yeah. About that long.
Over this past year, have you noticed changes in your mood—like feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you normally enjoy?
Um... no, not really. I mean, I'm not... sad all the time or anything. I still like doing the things I usually like. So... yeah, no. Just what I said before.

Around the time your symptoms started about a year ago, did anything else happen medically? Like, were you diagnosed with any new health conditions, started on any new medications, or experienced a significant illness or infection?
Um... no. Not really. I wasn't sick or... taking anything new. So... no. Just what I said.

When you were a kid, say in elementary school or middle school, did you have similar problems with paying attention, organizing things, or remembering to do tasks? Or is this really something new that started around that time you lost your job?

Um... I guess I've always been a little like this. Even back in elementary school. My teachers used to say I was smart, but... I'd always lose my worksheets. And I guess I didn't really read directions, I just sort of... rushed through them. I got in trouble for talking out of turn sometimes, too. And my desk was always a disaster... I could never find anything in there. So... yeah, I guess it's not totally new.

When you were working at the biotech job before you got fired, were you having these same kinds of problems with organization and remembering tasks there too, or did those problems mainly start after you lost that job?

Um... yeah, they were happening at the job, too. But... even since getting fired, it's... I don't know. It hasn't stopped. I've missed some follow-ups for new interviews. And... I had to step back from a volunteer project I was doing. So... I'm still unemployed. I just sort of feel like I can't... manage the basic steps to get my life moving forward right now.

When you're sitting down trying to focus on something, like reading or working on a task, do you find yourself fidgeting a lot, bouncing your leg, or feeling restless? Or do you feel like you need to get up and move around?

Um... yeah, I guess so. Sitting still is... hard. Like, if I'm in an interview, or a meeting, or... even just watching a movie... I get this feeling. It's like this pressure inside. I feel like I just... have to move. If I don't shift around or do something with my hands, it feels like I'm gonna crawl out of my skin. So... yeah.

When you think back to when you were around 10 or 11 years old, were you already having trouble sitting still and feeling that restless, fidgety feeling you described—or is that something that started more recently?

Um... yeah, I think I already mentioned that. Even back then... my teachers always said I was bright but... I'd lose my worksheets. And I rushed through everything. I talked out of turn... and my desk was just a mess. So... yeah, it's been like that for a long time.
